newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa plans travel agent commission cut.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa plans travel agent commission cut.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it plans to introduce a new commissions payment system for travel agents in the first half of 1997 as part of cost-saving measures.
The airline's chief executive marketing, Hemjoe Klein, said the new system was part of moves to reduce sales distribution costs from 25 per cent of total costs now to 20 per cent by 2000.
Lufthansa was under dramatic market pressure to cut costs and distribution costs were no exception, he told an agents congress in Berlin.

Klein said Lufthansa's distribution costs, including agents commissions, computer reservation system fees and other marketing costs had increased dramatically in recent years but he declined to disclose any absolute figures.
Agents' earnings should reflect quality of service and sales performance instead of the present standard nine percent payment on all airline ticket sales, he added.
But he stressed Lufthansa had not yet decided how much to reduce commissions and first wanted to discuss new payments systems with travel agents associations.
Klein said the airline aimed to have a new structure agreed by December for introduction in the first half of 1997.

The Lufthansa Internet service InfoFlyway, which allows consumers to make direct online bookings, was generating 50,000-60,000 consumer contacts a day but had not yet registered any bookings, he noted.

Figures released by the German independent agents association ASR showed travel agents sold 6.36 billion marks worth of Lufthansa tickets last year, which represented 95 percent of Lufthansa overall ticket sales.
ASR president Klaus Laepple said no one wanted "American conditions" in Germany and called on Lufthansa not to make net rates available to consumers.
But he accepted a new system was inevitable and called for sales volume to be taken into account.
Gerd Hesselmann, president of the DRV agents association, said he doubted a new commissions system could be agreed by December 15.
He said cost savings achieved by agents using technology such as Internet should be taken into account in the new system.
